rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing mockery, deception, and scheming to God means that He repays their agents in kind and makes their own traps ensnare them.
rows.anchor: “Alay etmek, aldatmak, tuzaklara karşılık vermek” gibi fiillerin Allah’a nisbet edilmesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrites think they hide their state and mock believers successfully, but God knows and informs the Prophet, making the hypocrites themselves objects of ridicule.
rows.anchor: gizli kameradan ekrana aktarılan kimseler gibi– kendilerini alay konusu haline getirmektedirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who consider themselves clever and believers foolish spend their life, reason, and will on misguidance instead of guidance and end their life's trade bankrupt.
rows.anchor: kendilerini akıllı, iman edenleri de akılsız ve ahmak sananlar, kendilerine emanet edilen hayat, akıl ve irade sermayesiyle hidayet yerine sapkınlığı aldıkları için hayat ticaretini de iflasla kapatmaktadırlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person's life direction depends not only on personal reason, will, effort, and acquired knowledge, but also on education and guiding influences from the merciful or Satanic.
rows.anchor: İnsanoğlunun hayat çizgisini belirleyen âmiller yalnızca onun kendi akıl ve iradesi, kendi çabasıyla elde ettiği bilgiler değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan has helpers among jinn and human collaborators; the verse warns people to notice whom they accompany and whose influence they accept.
rows.anchor: Şeytanın cin türünden yardımcıları olduğu gibi insanlar arasından edindiği işbirlikçileri de vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The broken covenant may be the primordial pledge to recognize God as Lord and serve Him, answered affirmatively at the sacred gathering, or promises made in worldly relations while invoking God.
rows.anchor: Bu söz ya ezelde “elestü birabbiküm”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Breaking promises is characteristic of hypocrites and others who share their traits.
rows.anchor: Münafıkların ve onların özelliklerini paylaşan diğerlerinin âdetlerinden biri de verdikleri sözde durmamalarıdır

rows.speaker: Bazı tefsirciler
rows.claim: Some exegetes restrict what God commands to be joined to particular bonds, such as kinship ties and reconciliation between spouses.
rows.anchor: “Allah’ın birleştirilmesini emrettiği şeyler”i kesip ayırmaları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers a broader reading: God wills the unification of religions, prophets, books, and humanity through monotheism, the reconciliation of fragmented things, and each person or thing occupying its proper place.
rows.anchor: Doğrusu bunu daha geniş bir çerçevede almak ve anlamaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Corruptors, sinners, and wrongdoers work to divide and fragment what should be joined.
rows.anchor: Düzen bozucular (fesatçılar) ve günahkârlar (fâsıklar, zalimler) ise bunları parçalamak ve ayırmakla meşguldürler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Corruption on earth includes material and spiritual disorder, pollution, unrest, pain, and calamity, historically caused largely by unbelievers, immoral people, tyrants, and sinners.
rows.anchor: maddî ve mânevî olarak düzeni bozan, çevreyi kirleten, huzursuzluk, acı ve felâketlere sebep olanlar genellikle inkârcılar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every sin is also corruption because it is forbidden by God and disrupts the earth's balance and order.
rows.anchor: aynı zamanda yeryüzünde bir kötülüktür, fesattır, dengeyi ve düzeni bozmaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who serve ego and Satan instead of God inevitably lose: they spend their lifespan on a transient world and forfeit eternal bliss.
rows.anchor: ömür sermayesiyle fâni dünyayı satın almışlar, ebedî saadetten mahrum kalmışlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening verse criticizes Jews, Christians, and pagan Arabs; Abraham's religion centers on God's unity, inward submission, exclusive worship, purifying the Kaaba, and its worship practices.
rows.anchor: İlk âyette yahudiler, hıristiyanlar ve putperest Araplar’a yönelik bir eleştiri bulunmaktadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham was made distinguished in this world and counted among the righteous in the afterlife as the greatest representative of this religion in his era.
rows.anchor: Hz. İbrâhim’in dünyada seçkin kılınması, âhirette iyiler arasında yer alması da böyle bir dinin kendi dönemindeki en büyük temsilcisi olmasından dolayıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham bequeathed the religion to his children and later generations; Jacob repeated the bequest to his sons, charged them to keep monotheism, and received their pledge to continue it.
rows.anchor: Hz. Ya‘kub’un da kendi oğullarına aynı vasiyeti tekrar ettiği, tevhid inancından sapmamalarını emrettiği; onların da tevhid geleneğini yaşatacaklarına dair söz verdikleri bildirilmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jews, Christians, and pagan Arabs who claimed Abrahamic descent yet rejected Islam and Muhammad thereby rejected the Abrahamic, Hanif tradition itself.
rows.anchor: İslâm dinini ve Hz. Muhammed’in peygamberliğini kabul etmemekle, temelde İbrâhimî geleneği, diğer bir deyişle Hanîf dinini de reddetmiş oluyorlardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an presents Muhammad's religion and the religions of Abraham and other true prophets as containing the same divine truths; Muslims are told to say they follow Abraham the Hanif.
rows.anchor: Hz. Muhammed’in getirdiği dinle İbrâhim ve diğer hak peygamberlerin getirdikleri dinlerin aynı ilâhî hakikatleri içerdiği bildirilmekte

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham and Jacob bequeathed a religion that was, in a general sense, Islam.
rows.anchor: İbrâhim’le Ya‘kub’un, oğullarına vasiyet ettikleri din de genel anlamda İslâm’dan başkası değildi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an indicates Jacob was Isaac's son and Joseph's father, recounting Joseph's dream, Jacob's grief and loss of sight, patience, journey to Egypt during famine, and recovered sight at reunion.
rows.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm’de de Hz. Ya‘kub’un, İshak’ın oğlu olduğuna işaret edilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an describes Jacob as righteous, as receiving revelation, and among God's strong and insightful servants.
rows.anchor: Kur’an’da ayrıca onun sâlih kullardan olduğu

rows.speaker: Tevrat
rows.claim: The Torah says God named Jacob Israel after Jacob wrestled with and defeated God; Islamic sources also use Israel for Jacob, while Muslim scholars offered differing explanations because the Jewish account conflicts with Islamic beliefs about divinity and prophethood.
rows.anchor: Tevrat’ta, Ya‘kub peygamberin, Tanrı ile güreşip O’nu yendiği için Tanrı’nın ona İsrâil adını verdiği bildirilir

rows.speaker: Müfessirlerin çoğu
rows.claim: Most exegetes take the opening em as an interrogative expressing rejection: Jews were not present at Jacob's death, so how can they claim his religion matches theirs when he reaffirmed Abraham's monotheism and took his sons' pledge?
rows.anchor: Müfessirlerin çoğu bu âyetin başındaki “em” kelimesinin soru edatı olduğunu ve red anlamı taşıdığını ifade ederler

rows.speaker: Fahreddin er-Râzî
rows.claim: Razi allows em to function as a conjunction: Israelite ancestors witnessed Jacob call his sons to Islam and monotheism, so their descendants know this and should not make improper claims about prophets.
rows.anchor: Fahreddin er-Râzî, “em” edatının bağlaç olarak da alınabileceğini belirtir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses criticize Jewish scholars who concealed scriptural information about Muhammad to protect their income and distorted religious texts from their true meaning and purpose.
rows.anchor: Hz. Muhammed hakkındaki bilgileri kendi insanlarından saklayan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criticism extends to anyone who hides truths by interpreting religious texts for gain and turning religion into a business.
rows.anchor: dinî metinleri çıkarları doğrultusunda açıklamak, yorumlamak suretiyle gerçekleri insanlardan saklayan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent verses to ground belief and conduct in sound knowledge and guide people to right conduct; concealing these truths or exploiting them for gain gravely frustrates that purpose.
rows.anchor: Allah, âyetlerini yalnızca insanlar inançlarını, amellerini, din ve dünya hayatlarını doğru bilgilere dayandırsın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even large material profits are insignificant beside this offense, so the verse calls them a small price; sacred values used for profit amount to eating hellfire, and God will neither address nor purify these people before painful punishment.
rows.anchor: işlenen suçun ağırlığına nisbetle son derece önemsiz kalacağından

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By distorting God's verses for worldly gain, they choose misguidance over guidance in this life and punishment over forgiveness and salvation in the next.
rows.anchor: dünyevî bakımdan dalâleti hidayete, uhrevî bakımdan da azabı bağışlanma ve kurtuluşa tercih etmiş bulunmaktadırlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing question asks whether they are so able to endure hellfire that they dared commit such grave sins, delivering a forceful warning.
rows.anchor: Onlar cehennem ateşine bu kadar mı dayanıklıdırlar ki böylesine ağır günahları işlemeye cesaret edebilmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As Israel marched under Talut to recover what it had lost, Talut used the Jordan River water prohibition to test the army's loyalty and strength of will; most failed, but the test also taught and trained them.
rows.anchor: kumandan su içmeyi yasaklayarak ordunun kendisine bağlılığını ve irade gücünü denemek istedi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talut attributes the test to God because obedience to the authority figure is God's command; alternatively, a prophet may have conveyed God's command to the commander, who implemented it at the right time.
rows.anchor: Tâlût’un yaptığı bu denemeyi Allah’a izâfe etmesi

rows.speaker: İbn Âşûr
rows.claim: The Torah's account omits the river test and instead recalls Talut's ban on eating bread until vengeance; Judges describes a water test in another war, so Ibn Ashur suggests the test may have been repeated and the Torah records only some instances.
rows.anchor: İbn Âşûr, II, 497

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Philistines were powerful and their commander Goliath was exceptionally large and strong; as the armies neared, fear and demoralization appeared among the Israelites.
rows.anchor: Filistîler güçlü bir düşmandı, başlarında da Câlût (Golyat) isimli çok iri ve güçlü bir savaşçı kumandanları vardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A small group of fighters with strong faith and courage tried to raise morale by recalling that victory belongs to those with the material and spiritual prerequisites, not necessarily the larger army, and by urging hope in God's aid for those fighting in His path.
rows.anchor: zaferin her zaman sayıca üstün olanlara değil, maddî ve mânevî şartlarını haiz olanlara ait olduğunu hatırlattılar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prayer for patience and firmness also served as an exhortation to resist and stand steadfast.
rows.anchor: Bu dua aynı zamanda direnme ve sebat gösterme konusunda bir telkin mahiyetinde idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because ordinary borrowing is necessary and abuse led to usury, the Qur'an permits loans and other lawful deferred contracts after forbidding interest; writing, witnesses, collateral, and trust help ensure timely full repayment and prevent forgetting or denial.
rows.anchor: faizi haram kılan Kur’an, gerek ödünç almak ve gerekse diğer meşrû akidleri yapmak suretiyle borçlanmayı helâl kılmış

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about salam, a sale paid for in advance with goods delivered later, for example at harvest.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas bu âyetin selem (peşin parayla sonradan, meselâ hasat mevsiminde teslim edilecek mal satma) işlemiyle ilgili olarak geldiğini söylemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes correctly generalize the rule to every deferred debt, since a specific occasion of revelation does not confine the ruling.
rows.anchor: âyetin geliş sebebinin özel olması hükmünün genel olmasına engel teşkil etmediğini göz önüne alan tefsirciler, haklı olarak bu âyetin bütün vadeli borç ilişkilerini kapsadığını ifade etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: Dört mezhebin imamlarının içinde bulunduğu çoğunluk
rows.claim: Most jurists, including the four school imams, and Ibn Atiyya treat the documentation measures as recommended safeguards, not binding commands.
rows.anchor: Dört mezhebin imamlarının içinde bulunduğu çoğunluğa göre burada, borcu güvence altına almak için öngörülen tedbirleri ihtiva eden emirler tavsiye niteliğindedir

rows.speaker: Taberî, Dâvûd ez-Zâhirî, Atâ
rows.claim: Tabari, Dawud al-Zahiri, and Ata consider the command binding: writing is obligatory and abandoning it is sinful.
rows.anchor: Taberî, Dâvûd ez-Zâhirî, Atâ gibi fıkıhçı ve tefsircilere göre bu emir bağlayıcı hüküm getirmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command for a scribe to write has been read as having literate parties write and exchange documents, while an able writer records the debt for illiterate parties; the verse supports written documents as evidence in Islamic law.
rows.anchor: Yazma emri aynı zamanda İslâm hukukunda yazının delil olduğuna, yazılı vesikanın ispat vasıtası olarak kullanılacağına dayanak kılınmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists differ on whether an approached scribe must write: some say it is individually obligatory, others say a collective duty when time allows; Jassas says writing itself is not obligatory, but one should teach it or find another writer to prevent rights being lost.
rows.anchor: Hanefî fıkıhçısı Cessâs’a göre yazmanın aslı bile farz olmadığına göre kâtibin yazmasının farz olması düşünülemez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether a scribe may charge depends on whether writing is obligatory, since religious duties cannot be paid work but optional acts may be; the author deems abstention impermissible when capable writers are available, especially if no substitute exists and rights may be lost.
rows.anchor: özellikle başkası bulunmadığında ve hakkın zayi olması ihtimali de söz konusu olduğunda yazmaktan geri durmalarının câiz olmadığını söylemek isabetli olsa gerektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing and witnessing are both required because they complement one another in securing the transaction rather than substitute for one another.
rows.anchor: Yazma ve tanık tutma birbirinin yerine geçmek üzere öngörülmemiş, amacı gerçekleştirmeye daha uygun ve yardımcı olacağından ikisi birden istenmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requirement for witnesses from among your men means they must be adults and Muslim men; jurists generally exclude non-Muslims from witnessing Muslim legal relations except a dying Muslim's will while travelling, arguing Muslims cannot reliably identify which non-Muslims will protect their rights.
rows.anchor: Şahitler çocuk olmayacak, ergenlik çağına gelmiş kimselerden olacaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Financial testimony requires either two men or one man and two women, as a precaution to protect rights rather than because women are intellectually or morally deficient; the second woman helps the first remember, and a woman counts as one witness.
rows.anchor: Diğer kadının işi, hemcinsinin unutması veya yanılması halinde ona hatırlatmaktan, hatırlamasına yardımcı olmaktan ibarettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a cash transaction is immediately completed, the writing requirement is lifted though witnesses remain recommended, because disputes can arise even without a term.
rows.anchor: Borç doğuran akidlerin peşin usulüyle yapılması, akdin hemen sonunda alacak ve borcun kapanması halinde yazma yükümlülüğü kaldırılmakta

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parties must not inconvenience or harm scribes and witnesses, even with unnecessary calls, pressure, or threats to distort the record; the verse forbids such conduct and calls them to fear God.
rows.anchor: İlgili âyet bütün bunları yasaklamakta ve tarafları Allah’tan korkmaya davet etmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Collateral is a material asset taken from the debtor and convertible to payment; Islam forbids using a human being as collateral, despite pre-Islamic practices that sometimes pledged children.
rows.anchor: İslâm’da rehin konusunun insan olması câiz değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When travel makes a scribe hard to find, a suitable pledge can replace writing; the Prophet's practice shows pledges are allowed outside travel as well.
rows.anchor: Rehin almanın câiz olması yolculuk haline özgü de değildir

rows.speaker: Hanefî ve Şâfiîler
rows.claim: Hanafis and Shafiis say a pledge contract is invalid if the collateral has not been taken out of the debtor's control; Malik says it is valid but binding only upon delivery, and the debtor can be compelled to deliver it.
rows.anchor: Hanefî ve Şâfiîler’e göre akid sahih olmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A creditor may not benefit from property pledged as security for a debt.
rows.anchor: Borca karşı teminat olarak alınan rehinden alacaklının istifade etmesi câiz değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among jurists who consider writing, dictation, and witnesses obligatory, some take the mutual-trust clause to lift that obligation, while others limit pledges as a substitute to travel; those who see security as recommended view the clause as reinforcing that advice.
rows.anchor: Yazma, yazdırma, şahit tutmanın farz olduğunu söyleyenlerin bir kısmına göre âyetin bu bölümü farz olma hükmünü kaldırmış

rows.speaker: İbn Âşûr
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur's wider reading, which the author endorses, extends fidelity to trust across all debt relations; without trust and responsibility, parties can wrong one another even when security exists.
rows.anchor: İbn Âşûr’un da işaret ettiği üzere güvene karşı ihanet etmemeyi, emaneti yerine getirmeyi bütün borç ilişkilerine yaymak daha doğrudur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who know relevant testimony may not conceal it; they should come forward even if not asked, while hadiths criticizing unsolicited testimony are understood as concerning God's rights or false testimony.
rows.anchor: tanık olanların bildiklerini gizlemeleri câiz değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Concealing testimony is a sin of the mind and will rather than an outward bodily act, which explains calling the heart sinful.
rows.anchor: Şahitliği gizlemek, bildiğini söylememek dışa vuran vücut hareketiyle değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sabr means enduring pain, difficulty, and hardship; musabara means enduring adversity between oneself and another or resisting an adversary more tenaciously.
rows.anchor: Sözlükte sabır “acıya katlanmak, zorluklara ve sıkıntılara göğüs germek” demektir

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi defines musabara as bearing adversity between oneself and another.
rows.anchor: Râzî, IX, 155

rows.speaker: İbn Âşûr
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur explains musabara as greater resistance than the person opposing you, such as an enemy.
rows.anchor: İbn Âşûr, IV, 208

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ribat literally means waiting and guarding where an enemy may arrive; technically it is staying firm in God's path, watchful and prepared against an enemy, from tying up horses ready for sudden attack, and murabit names a border sentry or soldier on duty.
rows.anchor: Daha sonra ister süvari ister piyade olsun, sınır boylarında bekleyen kimseye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After presenting core beliefs and practical duties such as pilgrimage and jihad, the surah closes with the disciplines needed to fulfill duties: patience for obligations concerning oneself, musabara for obligations involving others, greater resistance in jihad, and border vigilance against surprise attack.
rows.anchor: Yüce Allah kulun sadece kendisini ilgilendiren yükümlülükler için kula sabırlı olmasını tavsiye ederken; kendisiyle başkaları arasında gerçekleşecek olanlar için de müsâbereyi yani kararlılıkla direnmeyi emretmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's hadiths urge vigilance against enemies and border guards, promising them great reward from God and rescue from Hell.
rows.anchor: Hz. Peygamber de birçok hadiste müminlerin düşmanlarına karşı uyanık olmalarını, sınırda bekleyerek düşman saldırılarını önlemelerini emretmiş

rows.speaker: Bazı müfessirler
rows.claim: Some exegetes interpret ribat metaphorically as waiting after one prayer for the next, based on a Prophetic saying.
rows.anchor: bazı müfessirler buradaki ribâtı bu anlamda yorumlamışlardır

rows.speaker: İbn Âşûr
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur says the Prophet's prayer comparison is a simile: waiting for the next prayer resembles keeping watch at a border.
rows.anchor: İbn Âşûr, Hz. Peygamber’in ifadesinin bir benzetme olduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse can encompass both literal border watch and guarding oneself from evil through prayer; its final command to taqwa joins both, and omitting either leaves taqwa and success incomplete.
rows.anchor: âyetin hakikat olarak her iki anlamı da kucaklayacak mahiyette olduğu kabul edilebilir

rows.speaker: Muhammed Abduh
rows.claim: Abduh defines taqwa as protecting oneself from God's anger and punishment through knowing God and what pleases or angers Him, learned from scripture, Prophetic Sunna, and the exemplary early Muslims; steadfast defense of truth and vigilance lead to salvation and divine happiness.
rows.anchor: Muhammed Abduh buradaki takvâ emri ile ilgili olarak özetle şöyle der

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sources say the Prophet recited the final ten verses of Al Imran when rising at night for tahajjud.
rows.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in geceleri teheccüd namazına kalktığında Âl-i İmrân sûresinin son on âyetini okuduğu kaydedilmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Orphan property is delivered only after both marriageable age and actual financial maturity, since either can occur before the other; jurists differ on age from fifteen to nineteen and on separate ages by sex, and a state may select and legislate one view.
rows.anchor: Âyet malın teslimini iki şarta bağlamıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guardians test wards through suitable means, then when convinced of their ability to manage property, deliver it to its now mature owner in the presence of witnesses.
rows.anchor: Veliler ve vasîler uygun vasıtalarla kısıtlıları deneyecekler, rüşdün oluştuğuna kanaat getirdiklerinde şahitler huzurunda mallarını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guardians managing a ward's assets may take an appropriate customary or legal share or fee if they need it; if not, they are encouraged to serve freely for the ward and society, seeking God's pleasure.
rows.anchor: Kısıtlıların malları üzerinde tasarrufta bulunan vasîlerin, ihtiyaçları bulunduğu takdirde, örfe veya kanuna göre bu maldan uygun bir pay yahut ücret almaları câizdir

rows.speaker: Müfessirler
rows.claim: Exegetes say past-tense verbs describe resurrection and afterlife events as if already occurred, stressing their certainty.
rows.anchor: Müfessirler, bu ifadelerde, ba‘s ve âhiret olaylarının sanki vuku bulmuş kadar kesin olduğunu vurgulamak için geçmiş zaman fiillerinin kullanıldığını belirtirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verses may describe what happens to each unbeliever after death: the soul sees the next life, recognizes its worldly disbelief as error, and admits it before God; this happens to those already dead and will happen to future dead.
rows.anchor: ölen her insan gibi müşriklerin ruhları da bedenlerinden ayrıldıktan sonra ölümün ardından ikinci bir hayat daha olduğunu apaçık görmüş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those denying that they will be brought before God are losers; when death or resurrection suddenly comes, they lament their failures while carrying their sins on their backs.
rows.anchor: İnsanlardan Allah’ın huzuruna çıkarılacaklarına inanmayanlar, bunu yalanlayanlar hüsrana uğramışlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's people debate him and offer arguments against the clear reasoning from natural signs for God's unity; their arguments are omitted to show they are too baseless to mention.
rows.anchor: Âyette bu delillerin zikredilmemesi, onların anılmaya bile değmeyecek kadar temelsiz olduğunu göstermektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's question about disputing over God points to the absurdity of their claims that He has partners.
rows.anchor: de onların iddialarının saçmalığına işaret etmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although unstated directly, the people's threat that their gods would become angry and punish Abraham is inferred; Abraham disregards it but fears God, whose knowledge encompasses all and whose will governs harm and benefit.
rows.anchor: iyi bir mümin olarak, ilmi her şeyi kuşatan ve bu suretle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By asking whether they still fail to take heed, Abraham urges rational comparison between idolatry and the monotheism he proved, so they may recognize truth.
rows.anchor: doğru öncüllere dayalı aklî değerlendirme ve mukayese yapmaya, bu suretle hakikati bulup tanımaya çağırmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument asks which side is more entitled to safety: people who associate partners with the all-knowing creator of harm and benefit, or those who believe in God's unity and rule and follow His path.
rows.anchor: hangi tarafın, ilmi her şeyi kuşatan, fayda ve zararın yaratıcısı olan Allah’a ortak koşup isyan edenlerin mi, yoksa O’nun birliğine ve hükümranlığına inanıp yolundan gidenlerin mi güvence içinde oldukları sorulmaktadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase if you know indicates that only knowledgeable people can answer correctly and highlights the importance of knowledge for escaping false beliefs.
rows.anchor: yalnız bilgi sahibi olanların doğru cevap verebileceklerine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The predominant view is that Abraham himself supplies the answer to his question about which side is safer, since no other answer is possible.
rows.anchor: Ağırlıklı görüşe göre bu âyetteki ifade de Hz. İbrâhim’e aittir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who do not mix faith with injustice means Abraham's people believed in God but also associated other supposed deities with Him; injustice here means shirk, denying God's exclusive right to divinity and lordship.
rows.anchor: Âyetteki zulümden maksat, Allah’a şirk koşmaktır

rows.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
rows.claim: The Prophet says God's right over His servants is that they worship Him and associate nothing with Him.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın kulları üzerindeki hakkı O’na kulluk edip hiçbir şeyi kendisine ortak koşmamaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sound report says Muslims panicked, thinking they could not avoid all injustice in life; the Prophet clarified that the verse means the injustice in Luqman's warning against associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: Bunun üzerine Resûlullah âyete şu şekilde açıklık getirmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After criticizing baseless polytheist rules, these verses set out nine principal divine commands on monotheism and morality, then command following God's straight path as the encompassing duty; the invitation frames these as the sole correct and obligatory way.
rows.anchor: bu âyetlerde asıl benimsenmesi gereken başlıca ilâhî kurallar ve hükümler yer almakta

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Avoiding all association with God expresses Islam's central doctrine of divine unity and is the first condition of being Muslim.
rows.anchor: Bu, İslâm’ın ana ilkesi olan Allah’ın her yönden birliği inancının bir gereği olup müslüman olmanın da ilk şartıdır

rows.speaker: Fahreddin er-Râzî
rows.claim: Razi lists polytheist groups discussed in the surah: idol worshippers, star worshippers, adherents of Yazdan and Ahriman as gods, and those who attribute sons or daughters to God.
rows.anchor: Putperestler, yıldızperestler, Yezdân ve Ehrimen’in tanrılığını iddia edenler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihsan toward parents derives from husn, meaning goodness and beautiful conduct; placing it directly after God's unity underscores parental rights.
rows.anchor: Âyette bu buyruğun, Allah’ın birliğine inanmayı emreden ifadeden hemen sonra gelmesi, anne baba hakkının önemini gösterir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Killing children from fear of poverty implies doubt about God's abundant provision; the ban may also cover killing the unborn, not only pre-Islamic infanticide.
rows.anchor: anne karnındaki çocuğun öldürülmesinin de yasaklandığı dikkate alınmalıdır

rows.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
rows.claim: Hadith reports say the Prophet permitted coitus interruptus, the simplest form of birth control.
rows.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in, doğum kontrolünün en basit şekli olan azil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most scholars across the legal schools consider coitus interruptus permissible; this implies other non-harmful medical contraception is also allowed so long as no other prohibition is violated, since the Qur'an forbids killing a child rather than preventing conception.
rows.anchor: Çeşitli mezheplerin âlimlerinin çoğunluğu da azlin câiz olduğunu kabul etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because procreation is marriage's primary purpose, arbitrary avoidance of children for beauty or convenience is improper, especially when Muslim population growth is needed.
rows.anchor: kadının güzelliğinin bozulması, çocuğun bir ayak bağı telakki edilmesi gibi keyfî sebeplerle fıtratın tabii akışına müdahale etmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most contemporary scholars consider abortion forbidden at every stage of pregnancy.
rows.anchor: Günümüz âlimlerinin büyük çoğunluğu, hamileliğin hangi safhasında olursa olsun, çocuk düşürme ve aldırmanın haram olduğu görüşündedirler

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that pre-Islamic Arabs disapproved of adultery in public but practiced it secretly.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan nakledilen bir rivayete göre Câhiliye Arapları açıktan zina edilmesini hoş karşılamaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because fawahish is plural and no limiting evidence identifies only adultery, the author rejects narrowing the prohibition to zina; it covers shameful speech and conduct more broadly.
rows.anchor: bu yasağı zina ile sınırlamak doğru değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Explicitly forbidding both hidden and open wrongdoing shows that one who hides sin from people but not from God fears human censure more than God's command; forbidding even approach requires avoiding conditions that lead to sin.
rows.anchor: “yapmayın” veya “işlemeyin” yerine “yaklaşmayın” buyurulması, insanı kaçınılmaz olarak kötülük işlemeye sevkedebilecek ortam ve şartlardan uzak durmayı öngörmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on killing without just cause also declares life sacred and inviolable from Adam onward; haqq means a lawful, valid reason judged right by religion and reason.
rows.anchor: insan hayatının Hz. Âdem’den beri dokunulmaz olduğunu ima eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although everyone's property is inviolable, an orphan's assets merit special care because vulnerability exposes them to abuse; total neglect can erode the assets, so proper care is permitted and implicitly encouraged as virtuous.
rows.anchor: “en iyi ve en güzel” (ahsen) kaydından anlaşıldığı kadarıyla ilgilenmek zımnen teşvik edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trade often brings injustice in measures and weights; since perfect fairness may exceed human capacity, the following limit of capacity indicates inadvertent errors are not blameworthy, and Razi reads the wording as requiring both seller and buyer to uphold fairness.
rows.anchor: burada geçen ifa kavramı tam olarak ölçüp tartmayı ifade etmekle birlikte ayrıca bir de kıst (adalet) kelimesinin geçmesinden anlaşılıyor ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Justice in speech includes every verbal relation, from reporting and contracts to advice and criticism, and excludes speech intended to wrong, hurt, or insult; the clause about close relatives warns against bias from affection or pity.
rows.anchor: âyetteki “yakınlarınız bile olsa” kaydıyla bu hususta özellikle uyarıda bulunulmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's covenant means all duties He imposes; Muslims have pledged to follow His rules, and the command also covers keeping lawful promises to people.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın ahdinden maksat, O’nun kullarına yüklediği her türlü vazifelerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight-path command encompasses all previous commands and prohibitions; other paths are ways of thinking and living contrary to Islam that lead people away from God's path and true religion.
rows.anchor: 153. âyetin bu kısmı yukarıdaki bütün emir ve yasakları kapsamakta

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians had openly believed in Moses, so Pharaoh's words about believing without his permission are a threat, not a question; his promised punishments make this clear.
rows.anchor: sözü, bir soru olmayıp tehditten ibarettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's claim that they needed his permission to believe shows he asserted control over all their behavior and beliefs and suppressed their consciences.
rows.anchor: onların her türlü tutum ve davranışlarına hükmettiğini, vicdanlarını baskı altında tuttuğunu göstermektedir

rows.speaker: Fahreddin er-Râzî
rows.claim: Razi says the public defeat caused political anxiety: Pharaoh feared the people would follow the magicians and Moses, so he alleged a prior conditional agreement and trap to discredit Moses' victory; his unspoken concern was losing unpaid labor.
rows.anchor: Fahreddin er-Râzî’ye göre Firavun’un Mûsâ karşısındaki bu yenilgisi, onda aynı zamanda siyasî bir endişe de doğurdu
